name: Escape Zombie Control
description: A blocked Zombie pummel can be reset by preserving guard, withdrawing the pummeling hand and rebuilding Mission Control or ordinary inside frames.
summary: A blocked Zombie pummel can be reset by preserving guard, withdrawing the pummeling hand and rebuilding Mission Control or ordinary inside frames.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Zombie, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. Zombie is an arm-clearing action from facing guard. The guard player is not escaping a lockdown turtle shell, and turning to turtle is not required.

The bottom player has broken posture and supports a high Mission Control leg. The top player's hand or forearm is still obstructing the intended arm isolation. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): The hand pummel stalls; what can you recover first?
flashcards.answer: Withdraw the failed pummel and preserve guard with an inside frame and short hip escape rather than forcing the clamped arm.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder frame and inside knee room

plausible: Tighten ankle hold; forearm outside
Overhook before their hand clears

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): What must loosen before lowering the Mission Control leg?
flashcards.answer: Release any loaded neck or arm connection before lowering the controlling leg into an ordinary guard reset.

plausible: Withdraw hand; retain high-leg grip
Free hand lets go; high leg taut
trap: Release knee hug; keep pulling head

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): What lets the high knee lower comfortably?
flashcards.answer: Change your hip angle so the leg lowers through space rather than dragging the ankle against a stationary knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Hip motion clears the lowering path

plausible: Keep hips flat; haul the foot down
Straighten leg into their shoulder
trap: Lower ankle before letting grip go

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): Where should the pummeling forearm go during recovery?
flashcards.answer: The withdrawn hand becomes a useful inside frame so chest pressure cannot replace the failed arm exchange.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside, in front of their shoulder

plausible: Around the far side of their back
On mat outside your own shoulder

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): What should the hip escape recover?
flashcards.answer: A short shrimp behind the frame admits the inside knee and rebuilds a facing guard barrier.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee between your torso and theirs

plausible: Both knees behind you in turtle
Foot high before knee room returns
trap: Knee beside hip, outside torso gap

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): When is another Zombie attempt well set up?
flashcards.answer: Re-establish Mission Control posture control and a supported knee before using the free hand for another pummel.

plausible: Opponent upright with both frames in
Foot high, but knee drifting back
trap: Wrist exposed; your high leg slipped

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): Which exchange is actually being reset?
flashcards.answer: Zombie works on the opponent's hand and arm from Mission Control; the bottom player is already facing the opponent.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing hand pummel under a high leg

plausible: Knee hug round the isolated arm
Regrip around the cleared head
trap: Second leg closes after hand clears

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): With the pummel stalled, how can you retain facing guard?
flashcards.answer: The failed pummel leaves a guard-retention problem; frames and inside knees can be restored without turning away.

plausible: Turn to knees before adding frames
Keep high leg alone as chest enters
trap: Keep arm wrap with knees outside

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): Where should your forearm resist the pummel early?
flashcards.answer: Maintain an inside forearm so the bottom player's hand cannot easily lift yours out toward the mat.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside before their hand gets under

plausible: Outside their hip, elbow flared
Behind their head, hand hidden
trap: Across chest with wrist past elbow

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): How should the hand and elbow recover together?
flashcards.answer: Recover hand and elbow together instead of leaving the wrist exposed beyond a fixed elbow.
flashcards.answer_line: Hand and elbow return through slack

plausible: Only wrist in; elbow pinned outside
Straighten elbow with hand held
trap: Turn chest away to drag elbow in

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): Which cue calls for an early inside-hand recovery?
flashcards.answer: The hand-first pummel attacks the opening under your hand; respond before the bottom player's knee hug encloses the arm.

plausible: Their free foot settles on the floor
Their high leg lowers to your waist
trap: Their hand returns to shoulder frame

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): Where should the recovered elbow finish?
flashcards.answer: An elbow recovered toward the ribs can frame inside before the New York knee hug fixes it outside.
flashcards.answer_line: By ribs, inside their arm wrap

plausible: Elbow flared past knee, palm down
Hand on collarbone; elbow outside
trap: Past their shoulder in a head wrap

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): What must happen before you lift the chest?
flashcards.answer: Posture recovery follows arm clearance and an opened high leg; the hand pummel alone does not release the upper body.

plausible: Move hand; shoulder stays fixed
Widen knees; neck remains enclosed
trap: Recover arm; high leg remains taut
